title: Measles Cases in the U.S. Are at a 35-Year High
snippet:
Editor at Large

Measles is an old scourge that’s rapidly re-emerging as a new one. According to numbers released by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) on July 24, there have been 2,318 cases of measles reported nationwide so far in this year, already exceeding the 2,289 cases reported in all of 2025. The current figure is the highest incidence of measles in 35 years, a record set back in 1991 when there were 9,643 U.S. cases. [...] That much of a drop in vaccination coverage creates pockets for viruses, like the one that causes measles, to spread. Of measles cases so far in 2026 and for the entirety of last year, 93% have been among unvaccinated children, 3% were among children who received just one vaccine dose, and 4% were among kids who received both. This year, 7% of those cases resulted in hospitalizations. There have been no deaths so far this year, but there were three in 2025—one of them an unvaccinated adult, and [...] It wasn’t long ago that measles cases were extremely rare in the U.S. In 1963, the first measles vaccine was introduced in the U.S., and decades of steady administration of the shot eventually led to the country being declared measles-free in 2000. There were some scattered infections in the ensuing years—56 cases in 2003, 55 in 2012, 13 in 2020. But this year and last year, the numbers have exploded.

snippet: While the region has made significant progress towards protecting populations from measles, some countries have gone further. ## Vaccine development [...] measles virus

## Pre-vaccine era

Francis Home, a Scottish physician, demonstrated in 1757 that measles is caused by an infectious agent in the blood of patients.

In 1912, measles became a nationally notifiable disease in the United States, requiring U.S. healthcare providers and laboratories to report all diagnosed cases. In the first decade of reporting, an average of 6,000 measles-related deaths were reported each year. [...] Measles vaccine is usually combined with mumps and rubella (MMR), or combined with mumps, rubella and varicella (MMRV).

## Measles elimination in the United States

In 1978, CDC set a goal to eliminate measles from the United States by 1982. Although this goal was not met, widespread use of measles vaccine drastically reduced the disease rates. By 1981, the number of reported measles cases was 80% less compared with the previous year.

snippet: In 2025, the U.S. had more reported measles cases, outbreaks, affected states, and deaths than in any year since 1992, and measles outbreaks have continued to occur in 2026. The pace of reported measles cases has fluctuated from early 2025 until March 2026, but there have been continual outbreaks and more states affected over that time period. title: Vaccine Skepticism Has Risen in the U.S.—And in Many Other Countries | Council on Foreign Relations
snippet: Measles outbreaks are among the most visible signs of a broader trend. Vaccine-preventable diseases are rising globally, risking the reemergence of diseases that had virtually disappeared in many countries. [...] Highly contagious diseases are the first to rebound when vaccination rates fall, providing an early alarm that is already sounding. The WHO announced in January 2026 that six European countries had lost their measles-free status, including Austria, Spain, and the United Kingdom—a shift driven by declining vaccination coverage. Canada lost its measles elimination status the previous year, and the United States is working to retain its own as cases surge. [...] Public confidence in vaccine safety has fallen in countries across all regions, with some of the steepest drops exceeding 20 percentage points. This includes Germany and Sweden in Europe; Morocco and Tunisia in North Africa; and South Korea in East Asia. Even in countries where confidence appears stable or improving, national averages can obscure important internal inequities.
